en: The Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom. Om. Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Perfection of Wisdom.
The Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara [contemplated] the profound...
While practicing the course of the perfection of wisdom,
he looked down and beheld those five aggregates.
He saw them as empty of intrinsic nature.
Here, Śāriputra, form is emptiness,
and emptiness itself is form.
Emptiness is not separate from form;
form is not separate from emptiness.
Whatever is form, that is emptiness.
That which is emptiness is form.
Even so are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Here, Śāriputra, all phenomena have the characteristic of emptiness.
Unarisen, unceasing, not impure, not pure, not deficient, and not complete.
Therefore, Śāriputra, in emptiness there is no form,
no sensation, no perception, no mental formations, and no consciousness.
There is no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects;
and no visual element, up to and including no mental-consciousness element.

There is no ignorance, nor the destruction of ignorance, up to and including no old age and death, nor the destruction of old age and death; there is no suffering, no origin, no cessation, and no path;
there is no knowledge, no attainment, and no non-attainment.
Therefore, Śāriputra, because there is no attainment, a bodhisattva,
relying on the perfection of wisdom, dwells with no obscuration of mind.
Because there is no obscuration of mind, he is without fear.
Having transcended all perversions, he has reached the ultimate nirvana.
All Buddhas established throughout the three times,
relying upon the perfection of wisdom, [attain] the unsurpassed...
They have fully awakened to perfect enlightenment.
Therefore, it should be known that the perfection of wisdom is the great mantra,
the mantra of great knowledge, the unsurpassed mantra.
This mantra is peerless; it pacifies all suffering because it is true and not false.
This mantra has been proclaimed in the *Prajñāpāramitā*: namely—*Oṃ gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā*.
Thus concludes the Noble Heart of the Perfection of Wisdom.
